CONS-22: Differs only under disk exhaustion (below 100 MiB free) or a coins-DB read error. Healthy P2P or RPC input cannot reach it; clients see only process availability under that fault.
CONS-26: Accepted and rejected bytes are identical: the new check rejects only bytes the old read must reject a few bytes later, with the same exception type and peer handling. Only allocation and timing differ, which only stress probes can measure.
CONS-30: Only a wallet name containing an encoded NUL (%00) differs. Wallet files cannot contain NUL, and every well-formed name decodes identically. Covers P2P-39 (same decoder).
DKG-04: An abuse-quota exception. Canonical, unique honest DKG messages stay below the shared 2×size cap under both keyings (NodeId vs proTxHash, charge-before vs after the duplicate check). Only a verified MN that floods duplicates or reconnects to reset its quota can see the difference.
DKG-14: The custom LLMQ size options exist only in regtest and devnet params construction; mainnet quorum sizes already fit 400. Under -releaseprofile=23.1 on regtest the v24 refusal applies as a declared debug-option limit.
EVO-18: Bounded proof (GPT r2). For any valid parent after mainnet's first non-null coinbase ChainLock, both releases enforce non-null and child_diff ≤ parent_diff + 1, so the new range and ancestor guard cannot fire. Equivalence holds for extensions and reorgs above that history. The first-candidate and corrupt-parent cases keep v24's null-ancestor guard as a malformed-input exception; a null dereference is not reproduced.
SIG-11: Requires a quorum-signed ISDLOCK whose inputs differ from the locked tx. An ordinary peer cannot produce one without breaking quorum signature verification, and honest quorums sign the inputs in vin order. The exception assumes honest signing.
SIG-20: Contribution verification sets are identical for every non-empty input. Only the empty post-filter path differs, where v23 can leave a future unfulfilled; that is visible only to a deliberately arranged fault.
MPIX-03: Mainnet and regtest defaults are identical: standardness is always required, and mainnet refuses -acceptnonstdtxn=1. Only the testnet and devnet defaults differ, and those networks are pinned to v24, with no v23 override outside regtest.
P2P-30: PID-file ownership after a partial initialisation is process bookkeeping, not part of any peer or RPC contract. On normal operation both releases own and remove their PID file.
RPC-07: Only an RFC 3986-invalid URI differs: v23 dereferences a null parse result, v24 answers HTTP 400. Correct REST clients see identical behaviour; the exception covers only the null guard.
RPC-08: Race elimination: v24's coherent tip and UTXO snapshot is one of the responses v23 can give, and no valid client can require v23's inconsistency.
RPC-09: Shutdown lifecycle only: waiting for in-flight replies yields an outcome v23 can also produce. Method and result contracts are unchanged.
RPC-17: mockscheduler refuses non-mockable chains before forwarding in both releases, so it is unreachable on mainnet. On regtest the added synchronisation yields one of the schedules v23 can produce.
RPC-47: Only counts that make v23's mixed-width iterator arithmetic undefined differ; every count with a defined v23 result returns the same object sequence.
WAL-23: v23's sethdseed path writes a plaintext HD seed into an encrypted wallet that neither release can reload. The importer reports such files as corrupt rather than recreating the broken writer. Successful RPC result shapes are unchanged.
WAL-25: Applies only to malformed or mixed-format wallet files: corrupt HD-chain records and undeserialisable descriptors (a v23 abort becomes a v24 load error), and legacy records inside a descriptor wallet (v23 tolerated some, e.g. a valid defaultkey). Wallets written by either release's descriptor code contain no legacy records.
WAL-30: Both releases skip transactions older than the earliest key time minus the same window. v24 skips only a startup rescan that would find nothing under that shared model. The explicit full-rescan option (WAL-26) stays profiled.
WAL-32: Coin selection is randomised and unspecified in both releases, so only the inputs, change and fee of a given selection differ. Explicit-input options, errors, fee units and fully-mixed requirements are profiled elsewhere.
WAL-34: Both releases fund only from the requested fee-source address and produce v23-valid transactions; neither promises a particular input subset. Source-address, error and signing semantics are profiled (RPC-43).
WAL-44: Pruning during -loadblock changes only intermediate progress and disk use. The final chain state and the validation results of imported blocks are identical.
WAL-45: With -fastprune, v23 loops without bound on a block of 64 KiB or more, allocating until it runs out of memory. A non-terminating branch is not a behaviour to reproduce.
